title: Vapour pressure of an ideal solution
back: $p_1$ and $p_2$ are straight lines ($p_i=x_ip_i^\circ$); their sum, $p_\text{total}$, is a straight line between $p_1^\circ$ and $p_2^\circ$.

title: Positive and negative deviation
back: Positive: curves above the ideal lines, total has a maximum → minimum-boiling azeotrope. Negative: below, with a minimum → maximum-boiling azeotrope.

title: Elevation of boiling point
back: The solution's vapour pressure is lower, so it reaches 1 atm at a higher temperature: $\Delta T_b=T_b-T_b^\circ=K_bm$.

title: Depression of freezing point
back: Freezing point = where liquid and solid have the same vapour pressure. The solution curve meets the solid curve lower: $\Delta T_f=K_fm$.

title: Osmosis and osmotic pressure
back: Solvent flows through the semipermeable membrane into the solution. The pressure that just stops it is $\pi=CRT$. More than $\pi$ gives reverse osmosis.

title: Raoult's law
legend: x_1 = mole fraction of 1 in the liquid
back: In words: each volatile component contributes in proportion to its mole fraction.

title: Henry's law
legend: p = partial pressure of the gas
x = mole fraction of gas in solution
back: In words: more pressure, more gas dissolves. A higher $K_H$ means a **less** soluble gas.

title: Relative lowering of vapour pressure
legend: x_2 = mole fraction of the non-volatile solute
back: In words: the fractional drop in vapour pressure equals the mole fraction of solute. It has no unit.

title: Boiling-point elevation and freezing-point depression
legend: K_b, K_f = solvent constants, K kg mol⁻¹
back: For molar mass: $M_2=\dfrac{1000\,K\,w_2}{\Delta T\,w_1}$. The freezing point asked is $T_f^\circ-\Delta T_f$.

title: Osmotic pressure
legend: C = mol L⁻¹, V in L
back: Best colligative property for proteins and polymers: measured at room temperature and large enough to measure.

title: van't Hoff factor
legend: n = particles from one formula unit
back: $i>1$: dissociation (NaCl ≈ 2). $i<1$: association (ethanoic acid in benzene ≈ ½).

title: Positive vs negative deviation
back: Positive: weaker A–B forces, ΔH > 0, ΔV > 0, minimum-boiling azeotrope. Negative: stronger A–B forces, ΔH < 0, ΔV < 0, maximum-boiling azeotrope.

title: Plus gives Minus, Minus gives Max
back: Positive deviation → minimum-boiling azeotrope. Negative deviation → maximum-boiling azeotrope.

title: The four colligative properties
back: All depend on the number of solute particles, not their nature. Osmotic pressure is best for proteins and polymers.

title: Henry's law in real life
back: Soda bottles are sealed under high CO₂ pressure; divers get the bends as N₂ bubbles out (helium mix used); climbers feel low O₂ at altitude.
